issues.legal_issue: A claimant’s right to use land without liability to pay assessment is an interest in property modified when abolition of the estate makes the land assessable, entitling the claimant to compensation if the statutory conditions are met.
material_facts: The claimant was not the holder of the abolished estate and sought compensation for rights affected by its abolition.
A consent decree gave the claimant and his brothers the right to own and possess specified lands without paying assessment.
The claimant enjoyed the lands free of assessment when the abolition law came into force; thereafter assessment became payable on them.
There was no material showing that the estate holder could collect assessment on those lands despite the decree, and the arrangement was not merely a suspension of land revenue.
No compensation for this modification was otherwise provided.
issues.conclusion: The right to enjoy the lands without liability to pay assessment was an interest in property that was modified by the imposition of assessment. The claimant was entitled to compensation under Section 14(1), with the amount to be determined on further inquiry.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the Bombay Merged Territories and Areas (Jagir Abolition) Act provides compensation to a person other than a jagirdar who is aggrieved by the Act’s abolition, extinguishment or modification of a right to or interest in property, where compensation is not otherwise provided. A right to enjoy land without assessment is more valuable than the right to enjoy it subject to assessment, so the change modifies an interest in property; it was unnecessary to decide whether that interest was itself a right in the property. Section 3’s abolition of jagirs and associated rights supplied the context for the change. State of Gujarat v. Vakhatsinghji Vajesinghji Vaghela was distinguishable because it concerned materially different statutory language and a concession rather than a right. Shapurji Jivanji v. Collector of Bombay did not establish that the right to collect assessment could never be given up; the decision proceeded on the basis that it could be relinquished by contract or legislation.

rule.if: claim_for_abolition_related_compensation and claimant_is_not_abolished_estate_holder and assessment_free_land_use_before_abolition and assessment_liability_imposed_after_abolition and not mere_temporary_suspension and no_other_compensation_provided

predicates.claim_for_abolition_related_compensation: A person seeks compensation for an effect of abolishing an estate or its associated rights.
predicates.claimant_is_not_abolished_estate_holder: The person seeking compensation is not the holder of the abolished estate.
predicates.assessment_free_land_use_before_abolitio: The claimant was entitled to use the land without paying assessment before the abolition took effect.
predicates.assessment_liability_imposed_after_aboli: After the abolition took effect, assessment became payable on the land used by the claimant.
predicates.mere_temporary_suspension: The absence of assessment before abolition was only a temporary suspension of a liability that remained enforceable.
predicates.no_other_compensation_provided: No other provision provides compensation for the relevant modification.

issues.definition: When a person who is not the abolished estate holder seeks compensation for abolition-related effects, had assessment-free use of land that became assessable rather than merely temporarily exempt, and has no other compensation provided, the output is that compensation entitlement exists.

issues.legal_issue: A right to receive payment from an estate is an interest in property when the payment is charged on the estate and is not merely the estate holder’s personal liability, so its abolition may entitle the claimant to compensation.
material_facts: The claimant was not the holder of the abolished estate and sought compensation for rights affected by its abolition.
A consent decree entitled the claimant and his brothers to receive an annual cash allowance from the estate.
The allowance was payable from the estate and was a charge on it, rather than a personal liability of the estate holder.
No compensation for the abolition of this right was otherwise provided.
issues.conclusion: The right to receive the cash allowance was an interest in property and was compensable under Section 14(1).
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the Bombay Merged Territories and Areas (Jagir Abolition) Act provides compensation to a person other than a jagirdar aggrieved by the Act’s abolition, extinguishment or modification of a right to or interest in property, where compensation is not otherwise provided. A payment right charged on the estate, rather than a personal liability of its holder, is an interest in property.

rule.if: claim_for_abolition_related_compensation and claimant_is_not_abolished_estate_holder and payment_right_existed_before_abolition and payment_was_charged_on_estate and not payment_was_only_personal_liability and no_other_compensation_provided

predicates.claim_for_abolition_related_compensation: A person seeks compensation for an effect of abolishing an estate or its associated rights.
predicates.claimant_is_not_abolished_estate_holder: The person seeking compensation is not the holder of the abolished estate.
predicates.payment_right_existed_before_abolition: The claimant had a right to receive payment from the estate before its abolition.
predicates.payment_was_charged_on_estate: The payment was secured or imposed as a charge on the estate.
predicates.payment_was_only_personal_liability: The payment obligation was only a personal liability of the estate holder and was not a charge on the estate.
predicates.no_other_compensation_provided: No other provision provides compensation for the abolition or modification of the payment right.

issues.definition: When a person who is not the abolished estate holder seeks compensation for abolition-related effects, had a payment right charged on the estate rather than only a personal payment claim, and has no other compensation provided, the output is that compensation entitlement exists.
